name: a file replaced by delete-and-recreate (upload to a temp name, delete, rename) is one new version: the old one stays restorable
description: INFOMANIAK-004 (Infomaniak): a WebDAV client that replaces a file by delete plus re-create lost kDrive's version history. Rules P10 and D2: an atomic replace within one pass is one update of the same file; the drive keeps the earlier version; no trash, no conflict on the other device. sync-chaos port-office-save-interrupted.

name: a file deleted in one pass and created again in the next keeps every earlier version
description: INFOMANIAK-004 (Infomaniak): delete then re-create across passes. Rule D2: the drive keeps tombstones and versions, so v1 and v2 stay restorable after the re-create.

name: a time with nanoseconds comes back at one documented precision, and the precision causes no churn
description: INFOMANIAK-004 (Infomaniak): times stored at 1-second precision broke tools comparing exact mtimes. Rules P6 and P12: times travel and are set on downloads; a rounding never makes a pass upload again.
pending: an encrypted drive keeps no file's modification time: a drive synced by name has no way to send one (Drive::put takes none) and lists only the upload's second (ObjectInfo.modified), so the named sync sets mtime_ns 0 and a download gets the download time. It needs a time in the put calls, the pointer and the listing (P6/P12 on encrypted drives)

name: the WebDAV and S3 gateway linking a replace to the file's version history
description: INFOMANIAK-004 (Infomaniak): the gateway's own behaviour (rule V1) is the server's; sync-chaos srv-s3-conformance runs rclone and the AWS CLI against the stack.
not_applicable: WebDAV/S3 gateway semantics are the server's (iso, rule V1, dc scenario srv-s3-conformance); AzDrive's folder sync does not go through the gateway
